objective: Attack the one-old-edge repair proposed in C01 using an explicit tree, with a complete critical-edge case split and an exact two-edit repair.

atomic_claims.text: The two parameter tables define a proper star six-edge-coloring of a 31-vertex tree H.
The ten critical old edges in the displayed tree are individually frozen under star six-edge-coloring.
No coloring of G=H+uv extending after at most one old-edge change is a star six-edge-coloring.
The explicitly displayed two old-edge changes followed by color 3 on uv give a star coloring, so this witness has old-edge repair distance exactly two.

assumptions: All vertices in the parameterized tree specification are distinct unless the notation expressly identifies them.
Finite simple undirected subcubic graphs; star means proper with no bichromatic four-edge path or cycle.
Hamming distance counts changed old edges, not the newly colored edge uv.
Only finite-graph-basic and finite-combinatorics are used.
risks: This is a counterexample to a proposed repair, not to the root's existential coloring statement.
No mathematical computation or external verification receipt is claimed.
The 32-vertex construction is not claimed to be smallest.
The two-edit upper bound concerns this witness only; no universal two-edit lemma is asserted.

failed_route_proposal.blocker: The universal one-old-edge repair proposed in C01 fails on the specified tree. Fingerprint is SHA-256 of UTF-8 route_id concatenated with |universal-one-old-edge-repair, no newline.
